plain: To make up something false, such as a story or evidence

webster.text: To frame; to build; to construct; to form a whole by connecting its parts; as, to fabricate a bridge or a ship.

more.text: To invent and form; to forge; to devise falsely; as, to fabricate a lie or story.
To coin; as, to fabricate money.

example.quote: Should this at any time happen, how easy would it be to fabricate pretenses of approaching danger!
